en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section First Chapter
The Discussion on Whether Some Things Exist: The Discussion on Whether Some Things, such as the Past, Exist.
Does the past exist?
"Something exists, something does not exist.
"Something has ceased, something has not ceased;
something has passed away, something has not passed away."
"Is it the case that some have set, while some have not set;
some have utterly set, while some have not utterly set?
One should not say so... [and so forth].
Is it the case that some of the past exists and some does not exist? Yes.
Then is it the case that some past phenomena whose results have not yet matured exist and some do not exist?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … “Some of the past exists, some does not exist”? Yes.
Are past phenomena that have ripened as kamma-results some that exist and some that do not exist?
One should not say so...
[and so on] ...Is it the case that some of the past exists and some does not exist?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then do past phenomena that are without result exist in some cases and not exist in others?
One should certainly not speak thus …pe… .
Is it the case that some of the past exists and some does not exist?
Yes. What exists and what does not exist?
Past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened exist;
past phenomena whose results have already ripened exist.
"They do not exist.
As for those past phenomena whose results have not yet matured—
do they exist?
“Yes.
“Then do those past phenomena that have already ripened as kamma-result exist?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Are those past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened existent?
“Yes.
“Then do those past phenomena that are without fruition exist?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Are past phenomena that have ripened as their result non-existent?
“Yes.
“Then those past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened—
do they not exist?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Are past phenomena that are without result non-existent?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened do not exist?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Are past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened existent?
“Yes.
“But have not those past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened ceased?
“Yes.”
If past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened have ceased, then indeed you should not say:
"Past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened exist."
Are past phenomena whose result has not yet ripened, having ceased,
existent? Yes.
Past phenomena whose result has matured have ceased—are they existent?
One should not say so... [and so forth].
Are those past phenomena whose result has not yet matured, having ceased,
existent?
Yes, they are.
“Past phenomena that have not yet ripened have ceased—
are they existent?
“One should certainly not say so…” [and so on].
Are past phenomena, whose results have matured and which have ceased,
non-existent? Yes.
Are past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened, having ceased,
non-existent? One should certainly not say so… [and so on].
Are past phenomena that have not yet ripened and have ceased non-existent? Yes.
"Past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened have ceased—are they non-existent?
"One should certainly not say so... [and so forth].
Are those past phenomena whose result has not yet ripened, having ceased,
existent? Yes.
Are past phenomena, whose maturation has ripened and which have ceased,
non-existent? Yes.
Regarding past phenomena that have partially ripened as kamma-results and partially not yet ripened as kamma-results, which have ceased:
can it be said that some of them exist and some do not? One should certainly not say so … [and so on] …
Should it not be said that "past phenomena whose results have not yet matured exist"?
“Yes.
“But surely, past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened will ripen?
“Yes.”
If past phenomena whose results have not yet matured will indeed ripen, then, indeed,
it must be said of them: "Past phenomena whose results have not yet matured exist."
Is it because past phenomena whose results have not yet ripened will ripen that they are said to exist?
Yes. Is it because they will ripen that they are said to be present?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … “Because they will ripen, are they present? Yes.
If one considers that present phenomena will cease, can it be said that they do not exist?
One should not say so... [etc. ...
Discussion on certain [doctrines] regarding the future and so forth.
Is that which is future existent?
Some is existent, some is non-existent.
Some is born, some is unborn.
Is it that some [factors] have arisen and some have not arisen;
some have been produced and some have not been produced;
some have become manifest and some have not become manifest?
It should not be stated thus … [as before] … Is it the case that some of the future exists and some does not exist? Yes.
“Are future phenomena that are subject to arising some that exist and some that do not?
One should not say so … [and so on] … “Is the future partly existent and partly non-existent? One should not say so.
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then are some future phenomena that are not destined to arise existent, while others are non-existent?
You should not speak thus … [and so on].
Is it the case that some of the future exists and some does not exist?
Yes. What exists, and what does not exist?
Future phenomena that are subject to arising exist;
future phenomena that are not subject to arising [also] exist.
Those [phenomena] do not exist.
As for future phenomena that are subject to arising—
do those exist?
“Yes.
“Then do those phenomena which are future and non-arising exist?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Are those future phenomena that are non-arising non-existent?
“Yes.
“Then those future phenomena that are subject to arising—
do they not exist?”
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Future phenomena that are subject to arising—
do they exist?
“Yes.
“But are not future phenomena that are subject to arising unborn?
“Yes.”
If future phenomena that are subject to arising have not yet been born, then indeed,
it should not be said: "Future phenomena that are subject to arising exist."
Are those future phenomena that are subject to arising and have not yet been born existent? Yes.
"Are those future phenomena that do not arise and are unborn existent?
"One should certainly not say so... [and so on].
Are future phenomena that do not arise and are unborn non-existent? Yes.
"Are future phenomena that are subject to arising, being yet unborn, non-existent?
One should not say so... [and so on].
Should it not be said that future phenomena which are subject to arising exist?
“Yes.
“But surely, future phenomena that are subject to arising will arise?
“Yes.”
If future phenomena that are subject to arising will indeed arise, then, indeed,
it must be said of them: "Future phenomena that are subject to arising exist."
Having accepted that future phenomena which are subject to arising will arise, do you admit that they exist?
Yes. Having accepted that they will arise, do you admit that they are present?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Because they will arise, are they present? Yes.
If one considers that present phenomena will cease, can it be said that they do not exist?
One should certainly not say so... [etc.
...The discussion on the existence of some things is concluded.
